# A ball times a power of two, one-limb center, finite core

Kernel `ball_mul_pow2_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: the oracle tests it, but Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, that contains $x c$ for every $x \in X$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x c : x \in X \,\}.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet. It is part of [`ball_mul_pow2_1_full`](ball_mul_pow2_1_full.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $r_x \ge 0$.
- $c$ is a power of two: $c = 2^n$ for an integer $n$.

## Target (not proved)

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $\lvert (x c) - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$; and when $c_x c = 0$ or $\lvert c_x c\rvert > \frac{\eta}{2u}$ and $r_x c = 0$ or $\lvert r_x c\rvert > \frac{\eta}{2u}$, the ball is exactly the set: every number within $r_z$ of $c_z$ is a $x c$ of that kind, so that $c_z \mp r_z$ are the least and the greatest $x c$.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked.

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition ball_mul_pow2_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall cx rx c : R,
  fmt emin prec cx ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  fmt emin prec c ->
  0 <= rx ->
  (exists n : Z, c = bpow radix2 n) ->
  let '(cz, rz) := ball_mul_pow2_1 emin prec tie_even cx rx c in
  fmt emin prec cz /\
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  (forall x : R, Rabs (x - cx) <= rx -> Rabs ((x * c) - cz) <= rz) /\
  (((cx * c) = 0 \/ (eta emin / (2 * u prec)) < Rabs (cx * c)) /\ ((rx * c) = 0 \/ (eta emin / (2 * u prec)) < Rabs (rx * c)) ->
   forall s_ : R, Rabs (s_ - cz) <= rz ->
   exists x : R, Rabs (x - cx) <= rx /\ s_ = (x * c)).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** midpoint-radius scaling by a power of two (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_mul_pow2_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_mul_pow2_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# A ball with a one-limb center times a positive power of two c (milestone2.md, "Scaling a ball by
# a power of two"): exact whenever nothing underflows. When the scaled center is above the
# smallest normal number N = eta / (2u) in magnitude (or the center is zero) and so is the scaled
# radius (or the radius is zero), both scalings are exact and the radius is c rx itself: the
# result is c X. Otherwise the radius is the number after RN(succ(RN(c rx)) + eta), which covers
# the eta / 2 that the center may have lost and the rounding of the scaled radius. N and eta are
# exact constants of every format.

cz = prod(cx, c)
rr = prod(rx, c)
am = abs(cz)
bc = lt(const up(eta/(2*u)), am)
zc = eq(cx, 0)
ec = or(bc, zc)
br = lt(const up(eta/(2*u)), rr)
zr = eq(rx, 0)
er = or(br, zr)
ex = and(ec, er)
su = succ(rr)
sw = add(su, const up(eta))
rw = succ(sw)
rz = select(ex, rr, rw)
```
